- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment, leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply smoothing or lagged decay to peak forecasts.
- In periods of high volatility or sharp sentiment swings, model tends to lag behind true price movements; add 1–2 day lead time correction for mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillations (e.g., alternating +1.0 and -1.0), model may misread trend direction; favor mid-range or weighted average of recent 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture early mean reversion; apply downward bias in first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.3) over 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate; add 2–3% upward bias to compensate for suppressed momentum.
